what: Two ways to run a model
title: Synchronous and asynchronous model runs
text: ModelsCloud models can executed either two modes: Synchronous (default): call model_run() R blocks server finishes, hands result. Simple, ideal quick models. Asynchronous: model_run(async = TRUE) returns immediately lightweight job handle. model keeps running server R session free things. fetch result later get_async_results(). Async exists long-running models — policy simulations, large agent counts, anything might take minutes. Blocking interactive session (hitting HTTP timeout) run painful; submitting job . vignette uses examples/toymodel2, toy policy/economic microsimulation whose runtime scales number simulated agents — can run either way.
code: connect_to_model("examples/toymodel2", access_key = KEY)

title: Synchronous and asynchronous model runs
text: Nothing special required. default (small) agent count model returns quickly, plain blocking call need: fine model returns seconds. much larger run won’t — async comes .
code: input  <- get_default_input()    # n_agents = 1000 result <- model_run(input)       # blocks until the server is done result$total_qaly

title: Synchronous and asynchronous model runs
text: Set async = TRUE. model_run() returns job handle right away: job result — receipt. Pass get_async_results() fetch actual output server finished.
code: input <- get_default_input() input$n_agents <- 1e7            # ten million agents — a long run  job <- model_run(input, async = TRUE) #> Async job submitted (executionId: 6a2a...). Retrieve it with get_async_results().  class(job) #> [1] "pexa_result_async" "pexa_result"

what: Option A — block until it’s done (wait = TRUE)
title: Synchronous and asynchronous model runs
text: simplest pattern. get_async_results() polls server returns job complete: can whole thing one line: wait = TRUE polls every interval seconds (default 2) timeout seconds (default 300). timeout reached job handle returned warning, can keep polling rather losing job:
code: result <- get_async_results(job, wait = TRUE) result$total_qaly result <- get_async_results(model_run(input, async = TRUE), wait = TRUE) # Wait up to an hour, checking every 10 seconds result <- get_async_results(job, wait = TRUE, interval = 10, timeout = 3600)

what: Option B — check once, poll manually
title: Synchronous and asynchronous model runs
text: default (wait = FALSE) get_async_results() checks returns immediately: job finished, get decoded result; still running, get job handle back, unchanged. check progress without blocking — work checks, drive polling loop: test inherits(result, "pexa_result_async") tell “still job handle” “finished result”.
code: result <- get_async_results(job)            # one check  while (inherits(result, "pexa_result_async")) {   message("still running...")   Sys.sleep(5)   result <- get_async_results(job)          # check again }  result$total_qaly                           # finished

what: Choosing the mode per call vs. for the session
title: Synchronous and asynchronous model runs
text: async decided per call model_run(). need reconnect switch modes: runs long, set async session default connect_to_model(), bare model_run() becomes asynchronous: connect_to_model(async = ...) sets default. explicit argument model_run() always wins, can still force single call back sync: resolution order : model_run()’s async argument → session default connect_to_model() → FALSE.
code: quick <- model_run(get_default_input())                       # sync job   <- model_run(within(get_default_input(),                           { n_agents <- 1e7 }), async = TRUE)  # async connect_to_model("examples/toymodel2", access_key = KEY, async = TRUE)  job <- model_run(input)             # async, because that's the session default result <- model_run(input, async = FALSE)   # sync, despite the async default

title: Synchronous and asynchronous model runs
text: ?model_run ?get_async_results ?connect_to_model Example: EPIC-R vignette — async real COPD policy model.

title: Example: EPIC-R COPD policy model
text: Policy models don’t take patient dataset; take set parameters. get_default_input() returns ready--use model_input — named list whose input element holds EPIC’s default parameter set: adjust list pass model_run(). Scalar controls underlying simulation — n_agents, seed, time_horizon — set top-level elements model_input; server expands onto simulator.
code: mi <- get_default_input() names(mi) #> [1] "input"  mi$input$global_parameters$time_horizon #> [1] 20

title: Example: EPIC-R COPD policy model
text: modest agent count model returns quickly, plain call works: model_run() returns list $basic summary ($extended request setting mi$extended_results <- TRUE).
code: mi <- get_default_input() mi$n_agents <- 1000  result <- model_run(mi) result$basic$total_qaly

title: Example: EPIC-R COPD policy model
text: realistic policy run — say ten million agents — submit job async = TRUE retrieve finishes: check progress without blocking, call get_async_results(job) : returns finished result run done, job handle unchanged still running. See Synchronous asynchronous model runs vignette full async workflow (manual polling loops, timeouts, session defaults).
code: mi <- get_default_input() mi$n_agents <- 1e7  job    <- model_run(mi, async = TRUE)            # returns immediately result <- get_async_results(job, wait = TRUE,    # block & poll until done                             timeout = 3600) result$basic$total_qaly res <- get_async_results(job) if (inherits(res, "pexa_result_async")) message("still running")

title: Getting started with modelscloud
text: connect_to_model() stores model path key rest session, don’t repeat every call. ’s optional (can pass model_path / access_key function instead) keeps scripts tidy. Model paths "<collection>/<model>", e.g. "examples/toymodel1".
code: connect_to_model("examples/toymodel1", access_key = KEY)

title: Getting started with modelscloud
text: toymodel1 predicts risk one patients sex, age, marker_value. Two functions cover workflow: get_sample_input() — example input can run -model_run() — runs model returns result result comes back native R data frame — class information preserved across network, can work exactly model run locally.
code: sample <- get_sample_input() sample #>   sex age marker_value #> 1   0  55          1.2 #> 2   1  62          2.4 #> 3   1  48          0.7  result <- model_run(sample)   # model_input is the first argument result #>   sex age marker_value    risk #> 1   0  55          1.2 0.05787 #> 2   1  62          2.4 0.27289 #> 3   1  48          0.7 0.04565

title: Getting started with modelscloud
text: models draw plots run. toymodel1, instance, produces barplot predicted risks. OpenCPU captures plot server, fetch get_plots() — retrieves plot draw . display , call plot() retrieved image: Calling get_plots(result) id lists ’s available; passing id returns plot’s image, plot().
code: result <- model_run(get_sample_input())  get_plots(result)                  # list the plots this run produced img <- get_plots(result, id = 1)   # retrieve the first one plot(img)                          # display it

what: 4. A policy model with default inputs
title: Getting started with modelscloud
text: toymodel2 small policy/economic simulation. Instead sample dataset exposes get_default_input() — ready--use set parameters can tweak running.
code: connect_to_model("examples/toymodel2", access_key = KEY)  input <- get_default_input() names(input) #> "n_agents" "time_horizon" "p_event" "cost_event" ...  input$n_agents <- 5000        # adjust any parameter result <- model_run(input) result$total_qaly

title: Getting started with modelscloud
text: prefer call connect_to_model(), pass model_path access_key directly. explicit argument always overrides stored value. can also store key .Renviron MODELSCLOUD_ACCESS_KEY; modelscloud pick automatically, bare connect_to_model("examples/toymodel1") enough.
code: sample <- get_sample_input(model_path = "examples/toymodel1", access_key = KEY) result <- model_run(sample, model_path = "examples/toymodel1", access_key = KEY)

title: Example: QRISK3 cardiovascular risk model
text: QRISK3 takes table patients. get_sample_input() returns ready--use example dataset (QRISK3 package’s bundled test patients, column names matching model’s API): Pass n get just first rows:
code: patients <- get_sample_input() head(patients) #>   patid gender age atrial_fibrillation weight height ethiniciy ... #> 1     1      1  64                   0     80    178         1 ... #> 2     2      0  58                   1     72    165         1 ...  nrow(patients) #> [1] 19 get_sample_input(n = 3)    # first 3 patients

title: Example: QRISK3 cardiovascular risk model
text: model_run() predicts every patient input returns data frame QRISK3 score columns added: result native R data frame, can summarise plot locally usual:
code: results <- model_run(patients) head(results[, c("ID", "QRISK3_2017")]) #>   ID QRISK3_2017 #> 1  1    17.22985 #> 2  2    36.01234 #> 3  3     9.84512 summary(results$QRISK3_2017) hist(results$QRISK3_2017,      main = "Predicted 10-year CVD risk", xlab = "QRISK3 score (%)")

title: Example: QRISK3 cardiovascular risk model
text: get_sample_input() feeds straight model_run(): QRISK3 prediction model: every call synchronous — model_run() returns predictions directly. model supports asynchronous execution, see Example: EPIC-R vignette.
code: results <- model_run(get_sample_input())

what: R Interface for the ModelsCloud Platform
title: R Interface for the ModelsCloud Platform
text: R interface accessing models hosted ModelsCloud platform — cloud repository health decision prediction models developed RESP Lab UBC. modelscloud provides clean, session-based workflow: supply API key model (via connect_to_model()), call model repeatedly without repeating credentials. Results returned native R objects (data frames, lists, etc.), class information fully preserved across network.

title: R Interface for the ModelsCloud Platform
text: modelscloud depends pexaclient, installed automatically.
code: # Install from GitHub remotes::install_github("resplab/modelscloud")

title: R Interface for the ModelsCloud Platform
text: examples use public examples collection — two minimal toy models can call shared public test key, signup required. toymodel1 toy prediction model (predicts risk sex, age, marker_value). models, get API key ModelsCloud platform.
code: library(modelscloud)  # Connect once — stores the model path and key for the rest of the session. # (Public test key for the examples collection.) connect_to_model("examples/toymodel1",                  access_key = "23b7bab3-118e-4516-b53c-91bca8e0082d")  # Get a sample input, then run the model sample <- get_sample_input() result <- model_run(sample) print(result) #>   sex age marker_value    risk #> 1   0  55          1.2 0.05787 #> 2   1  62          2.4 0.27289 #> 3   1  48          0.7 0.04565

title: R Interface for the ModelsCloud Platform
text: connect_to_model() optional recommended — called, subsequent functions inherit stored model path API key don’t repeat .

title: R Interface for the ModelsCloud Platform
text: Pattern 1 — connect , call freely (recommended). Every later call picks stored values. Pattern 2 — supply credentials every call. Skip connect_to_model() entirely.
code: connect_to_model("examples/toymodel1",                  access_key = "23b7bab3-118e-4516-b53c-91bca8e0082d")  sample <- get_sample_input() result <- model_run(sample)        # model_input is first — no keyword needed ak <- "23b7bab3-118e-4516-b53c-91bca8e0082d" mp <- "examples/toymodel1"  sample <- get_sample_input(model_path = mp, access_key = ak) result <- model_run(model_path = mp, model_input = sample, access_key = ak)

title: R Interface for the ModelsCloud Platform
text: Quick models run synchronously — model_run() blocks returns result. Heavier models (large simulations) can run asynchronously: model_run(async = TRUE) returns immediately job handle, fetch result later get_async_results(). toymodel2 toy policy/economic model. See “Synchronous asynchronous model runs” vignette full async workflow (manual polling, progress checks, timeouts).
code: connect_to_model("examples/toymodel2",                  access_key = "23b7bab3-118e-4516-b53c-91bca8e0082d")  input <- get_default_input() input$n_agents <- 1e7            # a large run  job    <- model_run(input, async = TRUE)      # returns at once result <- get_async_results(job, wait = TRUE) # block and poll until done result$total_qaly

title: R Interface for the ModelsCloud Platform
text: modelscloud thin wrapper around pexaclient, handles HTTP communication ModelsCloud API. Results travel wire RDS (R’s native binary format), object classes fully preserved — model returns server exactly receive R session.
code: modelscloud          pexaclient           ModelsCloud API        model package ────────────         ──────────           ───────────────        ───────────── model_run()    →   function_call()   →   POST /call/{model}  →  model_run()                                     ←   RDS response        ←  result                ←   raw bytes        ←      result    ←   readRDS()

what: Connect to a ModelsCloud Model — connect_to_model
title: Connect to a ModelsCloud Model — connect_to_model
text: Stores connection settings current R session. calling function, model_run(), get_default_input(), get_sample_input() use stored values whenever arguments explicitly supplied. need call per session. settings optional except model_path.

title: Connect to a ModelsCloud Model — connect_to_model
code: connect_to_model(   model_path,   access_key = NULL,   server_url = NULL,   async = FALSE )

title: Connect to a ModelsCloud Model — connect_to_model
text: model_path Character. Model identifier "namespace/model" format (e.g., "resp/epicr"). access_key Character. API bearer token. NULL, previously stored key () left unchanged. can also set MODELSCLOUD_ACCESS_KEY environment variable .Renviron avoid passing scripts. server_url Character. Base URL ModelsCloud server. Defaults "https://api.modelscloud.resp.core.ubc.ca/" never overridden. async Logical. Sets default execution mode session. actual choice made per call model_run()'s async argument; just determines model_run() async left unspecified. Default FALSE.

title: Connect to a ModelsCloud Model — connect_to_model
text: Invisibly returns stored model_path.

title: Connect to a ModelsCloud Model — connect_to_model
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ connect_to_model(   model_path = "examples/toymodel1",   access_key = "YOUR_API_KEY" )  # Async by default, custom server connect_to_model(   model_path = "examples/toymodel2",   access_key = "YOUR_API_KEY",   server_url = "https://myserver.example.com/",   async      = TRUE ) } # }

what: Retrieve the Result of an Asynchronous Model Run — get_async_results
title: Retrieve the Result of an Asynchronous Model Run — get_async_results
text: Fetches result job submitted model_run(async = TRUE). Pass job handle returned model_run() directly. default checks : job finished returns decoded result (original R class preserved, exactly like synchronous model_run()); job still running returns job handle unchanged, can call get_async_results() later poll. Set wait = TRUE block poll automatically job completes (timeout reached).

title: Retrieve the Result of an Asynchronous Model Run — get_async_results
code: get_async_results(   job,   wait = FALSE,   interval = 2,   timeout = 300,   access_key = NULL,   server_url = NULL )

title: Retrieve the Result of an Asynchronous Model Run — get_async_results
text: job job handle returned model_run(async = TRUE) (object class pexa_result_async). wait Logical. FALSE (default), check return either decoded result unchanged job handle. TRUE, poll job finishes timeout reached. interval Numeric. Seconds polls wait = TRUE. Default 2. timeout Numeric. Maximum seconds wait wait = TRUE. Default 300. Set Inf wait indefinitely. timeout job handle returned (warning) can keep polling. access_key Character. API bearer token. Falls back stored key MODELSCLOUD_ACCESS_KEY environment variable. server_url Character. Server base URL. Falls back stored URL.

title: Retrieve the Result of an Asynchronous Model Run — get_async_results
text: job finished: model output original R class preserved (raw server response attached invisible attribute get_plots()). still running: job handle, unchanged.

title: Retrieve the Result of an Asynchronous Model Run — get_async_results
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ connect_to_model("examples/toymodel2", access_key = "YOUR_KEY")  # Submit asynchronously per call, then poll manually job <- model_run(async = TRUE) result <- get_async_results(job) if (inherits(result, "pexa_result_async")) {   Sys.sleep(5)   result <- get_async_results(job) }  # Or block until done result <- get_async_results(model_run(async = TRUE), wait = TRUE) } # }

what: Retrieve Plots Produced by a Model Run — get_plots
title: Retrieve Plots Produced by a Model Run — get_plots
text: Models hosted ModelsCloud can generate plots side-outputs run (e.g. barplot predicted risks). get_plots() retrieves plots server; draw . display retrieved plot, call plot() (S3 plot method renders image). Pass object returned model_run() directly — server connection details carried along automatically. Called id, get_plots() lists available plots returns summary data frame. Called id, returns plot's image.

title: Retrieve Plots Produced by a Model Run — get_plots
code: get_plots(result, id = NULL, access_key = NULL, server_url = NULL)

title: Retrieve Plots Produced by a Model Run — get_plots
text: result object returned model_run(). id Integer character. plot retrieve. Use id column listing (-argument) call find valid values. NULL (default), returns data frame listing available plots. access_key Character. API bearer token. Falls back stored key MODELSCLOUD_ACCESS_KEY environment variable. server_url Character. Server base URL. Falls back stored URL.

title: Retrieve Plots Produced by a Model Run — get_plots
text: id = NULL: data frame summarising available plots (one row per plot). id supplied: plot image object, display plot().

title: Retrieve Plots Produced by a Model Run — get_plots
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # toymodel1's model_run() draws a barplot, captured server-side by OpenCPU. connect_to_model("examples/toymodel1", access_key = "YOUR_KEY") result <- model_run(get_sample_input())  # See what plots are available get_plots(result)  # Retrieve the first plot, then display it img <- get_plots(result, id = 1) plot(img) } # }

title: Get a Sample Input for a Model — get_sample_input

code: get_sample_input(model_path = NULL, access_key = NULL, server_url = NULL, ...)

Falls back stored key MODELSCLOUD_ACCESS_KEY environment variable. server_url Character. Server base URL. Falls back stored URL. ... code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ connect_to_model("examples/toymodel1", access_key = "YOUR_KEY") sample <- get_sample_input() result <- model_run(model_input = sample) } # }

title: Run a ModelsCloud Model — model_run
text: Executes model ModelsCloud platform returns result. arguments fall back values stored connect_to_model() explicitly supplied, typical session need call model_run() arguments (just model_input). asynchronous jobs function returns immediately pexa_result_async object. Use get_async_results() poll completion.

title: Run a ModelsCloud Model — model_run
code: model_run(   model_input = NULL,   model_path = NULL,   func_name = "model_run",   access_key = NULL,   server_url = NULL,   async = NULL )

title: Run a ModelsCloud Model — model_run
text: model_input Named list (data frame) input parameters pass model. first positional argument, model_run(my_input) works connect_to_model() called. NULL model uses built-defaults. model_path Character. Model identifier "namespace/model" format. Falls back value stored connect_to_model(). func_name Character. function within model invoke. Defaults "model_run". access_key Character. API bearer token. Falls back stored key MODELSCLOUD_ACCESS_KEY environment variable. server_url Character. Server base URL. Falls back stored URL. async Logical. Run asynchronously? TRUE, returns job handle immediately; retrieve result get_async_results(). left NULL (default), uses session default set connect_to_model() (FALSE unless changed).

title: Run a ModelsCloud Model — model_run
text: model output original R class preserved (e.g. data frame), deserialised RDS format. raw server response attached invisible attribute, get_plots() uses retrieve plots model produced.

title: Run a ModelsCloud Model — model_run
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ connect_to_model("examples/toymodel2", access_key = "YOUR_KEY")  # Run with model defaults result <- model_run()  # Run with custom inputs result <- model_run(model_input = list(time_horizon = 15, discount_rate = 0.03))  # Override async for a single call job <- model_run(async = TRUE) result <- get_async_results(job) } # }
